(men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers Scarlet Knights]] and the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon Ducks]]. ==Early life== Omoruyi was born in [[Benin City]], Nigeria and immigrated to Canada with his family as a one-year-old. He grew up playing [[association football|soccer]] and began playing basketball during his second year at [[Monsignor Percy Johnson Catholic High School]].{{cite web |last1=Hansen |first1=Chris |title=After a year on the bench, two veteran men's basketball transfers ready for their Oregon debuts |url=https://www.registerguard.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2020/11/09/after-year-bench-two-oregon-mens-basketball-transfers-ready-debut/6218491002/ |website=[[The Register-Guard]] |access-date=January 5, 2021 |date=November 9, 2020}} Omoruyi attended [[Athlete Institute|Orangeville Prep]] in [[Orangeville, Ontario]], averaging 16.9 points and 9.6 rebounds per game and earning Ontario Scholastic Basketball Association First Team All-Star honours in his final season. He played alongside [[Jamal Murray]] and [[Thon Maker]].{{cite web |title=Eugene Omoruyi Signs with Rutgers Basketball |url=https://scarletknights.com/news/2016/8/9/Eugene_Omoruyi_Signs_with_Rutgers_Basketball.aspx |website=Rutgers University Athletics |access-date=January 8, 2021 |date=August 9, 2016}} He competed for Advantage Titans on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit.{{cite web |last1=Hellman |first1=Sam |title=Pikiell: Omoruyi Versatility "Off the Charts" |url=https://247sports.com/college/rutgers/Article/Rutgers-Coach-Pikiell-Wing-Eugene-Omoruyis-Versatility-Off-the-Charts-74973122/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=January 8, 2021 |date=August 11, 2016}} Omoruyi committed to playing college basketball for [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]] over an offer from [[Loyola Ramblers men's basketball|Loyola (Illinois)]].{{cite web |last1=Carino |first1=Jerry |title=Rutgers hoops adds 2016 wing from Canada |url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/college/2016/08/03/rutgers-hoops-adds-2016-wing-eugene-omoruyi/88047048/ |website=[[Asbury Park Press]] |access-date=January 5, 2021 |date=August 3, 2016}} ==College career== As a freshman at Rutgers, Omoruyi averaged 2.4 points and 2.2 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=Eugene Omoruyi – Men's Basketball |url=https://goducks.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/eugene-omoruyi/10388 |website=University of Oregon Athletics |access-date=January 8, 2021}} On November 28, 2017, he scored a sophomore season-high 22 points in a 78–73 loss to [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]].{{cite web |last1=Fonseca |first1=Brian |title=Eugene Omoruyi Flashes Potential in Loss to Florida State |url=https://www.onthebanks.com/2017/11/28/16713880/eugene-omoruyi-flashes-potential-in-rutgers-mens-basketball-loss-to-florida-state |website=On the Banks |access-date=January 8, 2021 |date=November 28, 2017}} As a sophomore, Omoruyi averaged 7.9 points and five rebounds per game. For his junior season, he was named a team co-captain.{{cite web |last1=Breitman |first1=Aaron |title=Rutgers Men's Basketball Names Captains For Next Season |url=https://www.onthebanks.com/2018/5/31/17412428/rutgers-mens-basketball-names-captains-next-season-eugene-omoruyi-shaq-doorson-steve-pikiell-big-ten |website=On the Banks |access-date=January 8, 2021 |date=May 31, 2018}} During the offseason, he improved his shooting by taking 1,000 shots for six mornings per week. On November 11, 2018, he recorded a junior season-high 24 points and 10 rebounds in a 95–66 win over [[Drexel Dragons men's basketball|Drexel]].{{cite web |last1=Carino |first1=Jerry |title=Rutgers basketball: Eugene Omoruyi leads offensive explosion in romp of Drexel |url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/college/2018/11/11/rutgers-basketball-drexel/1942437002/ |website=[[Asbury Park Press]] |access-date=January 8, 2021 |date=November 11, 2018}} On November 23, Omoruyi posted 20 points and 17 rebounds in a 54–44 win over [[Boston University Terriers men's basketball|Boston University]].{{cite web |last1=Carino |first1=Jerry |title=Rutgers basketball: Omoruyi, defense enough to hold off Boston University |url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/college/2018/11/23/rutgers-basketball-boston-university/2077435002/ |website=[[Asbury Park Press]] |access-date=January 8, 2021 |date=November 23, 2018}} He averaged 13.8 points, 7.2 rebounds and 2.4 assists per game as a junior. He was an All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] Honorable Mention and Second Team All-Met selection.{{cite web |last1=Carino |first1=Jerry |title=Rutgers basketball: In an absolute stunner, Eugene Omoruyi to transfer |url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/college/2019/05/29/rutgers-basketball-eugene-omoruyi/1268151001/ |website=[[Asbury Park Press]] |access-date=January 8, 2021 |date=May 29, 2019}} For his senior season, Omoruyi transferred to [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] and sat out for his next season due to [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] transfer rules.{{cite web |last1=Schnyderite |first1=Richard |title=Eugene Omoruyi talks for the first time since his transfer |url=https://rutgers.rivals.com/news/eugene-omoruyi-talks-for-the-first-time-since-his-transfer |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=January 8, 2021 |date=September 24, 2019}} His decision to transfer from Rutgers was described by the media as unexpected.{{cite web |last1=Kratch |first1=James |title=No, you read that right: Rutgers' Eugene Omoruyi apparently wants out in shocking transfer push |url=https://www.nj.com/rutgersbasketball/2019/05/no-you-read-that-right-rutgers-eugene-omoruyi-apparently-wants-out-in-shocking-transfer-push.html |website=[[The Star-Ledger]] |access-date=January 8, 2021 |date=May 29, 2019}} On December 2, 2020, he made his debut for Oregon and recorded a career-high 31 points and 11 rebounds in an 83–75 loss to [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]].{{cite web |last1=Young |first1=Ashley |title=Eugene Omoruyi was worth the long wait for Oregon MBB |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/northwest/oregon-ducks/eugene-omoruyi-was-worth-long-wait-oregon-mbb |website=NBC Sports |access-date=January 8, 2021 |date=December 2, 2020}} As a senior, he averaged 17.1 points, 5.4 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.5 steals per game, earning First Team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] honors. Following the season, Omoruyi declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]].{{cite magazine |last1=Reubenking |first1=Dylan |title=Eugene Omoruyi Declares for the NBA Draft |url=https://www.si.com/college/oregon/basketball/eugene-omoruyi-declares-for-nba-draft |access-date=June 29, 2021 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=April 12, 2021}} ==Professional career==
